Tower of Outer Planes:
Start the party before the tower, maybe on a ship sailing to the island, and some crash happens, or they just meet up there and head to the island.  I want the party to get experience before entering the tower, so maybe they can crash in a nearby island that is uninhabited or takes a bit to find people who live there.  Or the island with the tower is very large, so it would take a bit to reach the tower.  



Each level has certain deities or single deity who are controlling or causing the effects of each level in the tower.  The party may or may not need approval from these gods through acts that symbolize the type of god and outer plane.  As they go up, the tower will get harder.  The tower has been made for millions of years, so ancient cool artifacts are scattered throughout, however some may be hard to obtain. Also the higher you go the cooler and most interesting/powerful artifacts you will be able to get.  Each level will have a plot and “arc” so it will take time to get to the top.  Each plot will symbolize the opposite of what the gods would want as said before.  The farther you go up, the less people that have been up there.  Nobody (to the party’s knowledge) has been to the top level. DM: there have been 7 people who have made it to the top.  They are known as the seven planewalkers, those who have proven themselves to make it to the top of the tower.  These people have insane powers, not all of them are friendly either. 
 
Party knows very little about the tower and who is in it.  A very few people have come back from the tower, unknown how to the party.
 
First level – Mount Celestia of the Seven Heavens
Information –
Large Mountain in level, with forests and wild lands, but the mountain is most of the area.  People live in towns across the area, all of these people (unknown to party) are people who have tried climbing the tower but ended up staying at the first level, or people who have been there from the start.  People seem to be close to immortals who stay in the first level, they age very slowly, but they cannot escape before the first level.  However, if anyone stays in this Level too long, they will be forever stuck in this level and must continuously please the gods of this level. 

The mountain of this level is larger than any regular mountain.  This mountain is about 50 miles tall, and some say those who reach the top can see the heavens.  The mountain becomes so steep that trees begin to grow horizontally.

General Ideas
The gods could draw their power based on the world's living beings (so the more hate and suffering, the more that the dormant gods gain in power, the more neutrality, judgment, and order, the more the new gods gain in power). Perhaps the ongoing political, social, and cultural conflicts, injustices, wars, rebellions, etc, in the world have created a breaking point for the dormant gods, causing the crazy plague god to wreak havoc. (needs to be more fleshed out, but the gist of it).

 Gods may draw power (or not necessarily power, but could just put high emphasis on popularity) based on how people remember them, as in, the more people that have knowledge, or are aware of a particular god, the more that god gains in power. So since the dormant gods are being slowly more and more forgotten by the masses, they are angry, with the plague god being the most forgotten of them all, resulting in the god giving punishment to the world.

 The main religion could be broken into multiple different sub-religions based on how each respective group of people interpret how good, neutral, or bad a specific god, or gods are. So for example, some may see the new gods or dormant as more evil, while others may see them as neutral or good. So multiple branches of the religion are created, and could result in holy wars, possibly. This could exist in more simpler terms too, with the main religion split into the dormant god followers (like a cult), and the new god followers.

4. They created the plague to create disorder and chaos so that the old ones could feed on it and get stronger and come back?



Specific ideas
Sacrifices, offerings, rituals
Some followers of the religion may cause some to see the plague as a good thing, as some sort of needed sacrifice to please the gods. This could cause much difficulty with finding a cure or stopping the plague as some try to stop the cure from being found so that a sort of “prophecy” is succeeded. These followers feel that anyone that would go against this is purely acting out of sacrilege and is to be punished by death. 


Various shrines of each of the gods (both new and dormant) could exist to give various offerings that may or may not actually please the gods. These shrines are usually staffed with some sort of cleric or priest that follows a particular god. The dormant god shrines could be found in darker, evil places of the world and aren’t as easily accessible, at least safely. 


Some rituals could be done to try and please these gods, but they would be heavily dependent on the region and individuals doing it, as nobody truly knows what the cosmic gods want. However, it usually would be based on some sort of cosmic sign that is found in the sky. This could be highly interpretative as well, where some might interpret the constellations to show something as simple as fire or water that must be used, or something more complex, like specific gems, crystals, particular bones, or even blood or souls/lives. Also the symbols used in these rituals would depend likely on the sigils or symbolism of the gods, or of the religion as a whole.
Followers, Clerics, Priests
Due to the nature of the gods being very unknown and ambiguous, the followers have grouped into various archetypes based on their race and/or geographic location and this changes how they view and perceive the gods. The religious colors that the priests and clerics wear, to the stories they tell and the services they provide, it all changes as nobody truly knows or understands the gods.


The clerics and priests act as messengers and direct connections to the gods (which likely wouldn’t be the case, but the masses think they do), which in turn has caused much of the political power to go to these appointed individuals, leading to much corruption and false pretenses that these people give.

Another idea is that clerics and priests are more of a taboo thing, as any attempts to tap into the communication/power of these gods result in bad things. The more they try to find what “truth” is among the gods, the more their minds and free-will are controlled, and madness/insanity occurs as their minds cannot take in what they are trying to receive. Could even become a sort of Viktor arcane sort of thing where the followers of certain gods are controlled in a cosmic sort of way. 
Rules, Commandments
Each god could have a specific theme that describes them, as other religions do (think of god of sleep, god of luck, god of thunder, etc). These could be as simple as one that people mostly represent to neural things like Justice, Judgement, Life/Death, War, etc, and other gods that may represent more chaotic things like Pain, Suffering, Debauchery, Destruction, etc. 
The religion as a whole, or particular gods could have commandments (or list of commandments), or rules that attach to each. These were made up by the religion of course, but its what they believe is correct to follow for these gods. Assuming the new gods are more popular, these would likely be commandments that are more neutral, but could be interpreted as otherwise. Some examples:
	1) Control must always prevail, no matter the consequence.
	2) Life is inconsequential in the pursuit of justice and judgement.
	3) The truth of the cosmos must be left, for the mortal man cannot comprehend.
	4) Evil and good do not exist, only order and disorder.

People believe these to be signs from the gods that they are very unhappy.

Some believe that once you die, you are brought into space and become one with the cosmos. They believe that each star in the sky is a dead soul, and brighter stars are represented as more important beings.
Once you are no longer alive, you are taken to a dimension of judgement, where you shall be either reborn and brought back as a new life, or you are thrown into what many believe is the realm of the dormant gods, a chaotic and evil place that would be similar to an underworld or hell. Each dormant god has a domain of hell that is believed, with each worse god going deeper and deeper into the layers of hell. Task:


Here is a bunch of random ideas I had for stories and dnd campaigns that I wanna collect into a few main storylines that I can utilize. Please organize all these story ideas into summarized descriptions that I could fit into a new story or use for inspiration.

Of course. Your notes are a rich tapestry of ideas for a fantasy world, blending political intrigue, planar exploration, divine conflict, and personal quests. Here are the summarized story concepts, organized for clarity and inspiration.

### 1. The King's Shadow (Political Thriller / Conspiracy)
A tale of courtly intrigue, hidden enemies, and a dark ritual masquerading as tradition.

*   **The Setup:** A prosperous city is thrown into turmoil after the beloved king is murdered. His young, naive child ascends to the throne, guided by a board of directors and a trusted family friend, the head of the scouting team known only as "Blank."
*   **The Hidden Enemy:** Unbeknownst to the court, Blank is the mastermind behind a sinister plot. He influences the new king from the shadows.
*   **The Inciting Incident:** The party is framed for a violent attack on a city festival. They discover the attackers are part of a clan performing a forbidden ritual.
*   **The Dark Ritual:** Inspired by *Fullmetal Alchemist*, the clan and Blank are creating markings on their bodies—an eye symbol surrounded by lines (| = 10, △ = 100, X = 1000)—through a ritual that uses human sacrifices. The ritual creates a zone of black quicksand from which there is no escape. The larger the mark, the greater the power gained, seemingly based on the Seven Deadly Sins.
*   **The Adventure Begins:** The party arrives in the capital city by boat, witnessing the bustling docks and learning of an upcoming festival with a grand prize. This festival is the site of their first major confrontation. An alternative hook involves a suspicious old man warning of doom at the festival.

### 2. The Celestial Spire (Planar Ascent)
An epic quest to conquer a mythical tower that pierces the outer planes, challenging both the body and soul.

*   **The Challenge:** A colossal tower exists on a remote island, with each of its 16 levels representing a different Outer Plane and its associated deities. The higher the party climbs, the more difficult and rewarding the journey becomes.
*   **The Levels:** Each level is a self-contained world with its own challenges, plots, and guardians (e.g., Level 1: Mount Celestia's paradise town; Level 2: Bytopia's twin islands). The party must often appease the local deity to proceed.
*   **The Prize:** Scattered throughout the tower are ancient and powerful artifacts. Those who reach the top are granted a single wish by the gods, but with a hidden "catch."
*   **The Guardians:** Only seven individuals, the "Seven Planewalkers," have ever reached the top. They are immensely powerful and may see the party as a threat, attacking to "protect" them from the gods' curse or to prevent them from ascending further.
*   **The Secrets:** The tower is a divine test created to judge mortals. Its purpose is shrouded in mystery. The ultimate goal could be to join the Planewalkers, destroy the tower, or confront the gods themselves. A final boss could be the Dark Six, a group of powerful demigods.

### 3. Echoes of the Old Gods (Divine War)
A world-spanning conflict rooted in a forgotten history of gods, where faith itself is a battlefield.

*   **The Cosmic Struggle:** Two factions of gods are in conflict: the ancient, chaotic **Dormant Gods** (of hate, suffering, and disorder) and the newer, orderly **New Gods** (of justice, neutrality, and control).
*   **Power of Belief:** The gods draw power from mortals, either through collective emotions (hate fuels the old gods, order fuels the new) or through worship and memory (forgotten gods grow angry). A devastating plague is a weapon unleashed by the Dormant Gods to create chaos and regain their strength.
*   **A Fractured Faith:** The main religion is split. Followers of the Dormant Gods are often seen as a dangerous cult, while the New Gods' faith is divided into sub-religions, leading to potential holy wars.
*   **The Clergy's Curse:** Attempting to communicate with the gods can lead to madness and loss of free will. Clerics are viewed with suspicion, seen as either corrupt messengers or dangerously insane individuals.
*   **World Details:** The conflict is reflected in society, with commandments emphasizing control, the insignificance of life for justice, and the incomprehensibility of cosmic truth. Sigils, constellations, and celestial events are interpreted as signs from the divine.

### 4. A Soul's Price (Personal Quest)
A dark, emotional quest centered on obsession, resurrection, and the terrible price of cheating death.

*   **The Villain's Motivation:** A powerful individual (a Rakshasa, Hag, or grieving person) seeks to resurrect a dead loved one.
*   **Methods of Madness:**
    *   **Kidnapping:** Abducting a noble for a ritual sacrifice.
    *   **Invasion:** Creating a Philosopher's Stone-like object by sacrificing thousands.
    *   **Terrorism:** Using fear to force officials to grant a resurrection item.
    *   **Religious Zeal:** Performing a ritual that curses local wildlife to protect the ceremony.
    *   **Political Conspiracy:** Reviving a dark entity to gain power.
*   **Potential Targets:** The revived being could be a Vampire, Medusa, Giant, Efreeti, or Devil.
*   **A Specific Tale:** A tribe of Lizardfolk in a swamp seeks to revive their ancient, sealed king, believing a human spellcaster can help them, unaware they are to be the final sacrifice.
*   **Allies & Monsters:** Potential allies include a Treant or Djinni. The villain might command monstrous allies like Weretigers, Hellhounds, or Displacer Beasts.

### 5. Whispers in the Arcane City (Urban Mystery)
A self-contained adventure that begins with a strange occurrence in a magically-protected city.

*   **The Hook:** While staying at an inn, the party is awakened by a noise. Investigating, they find a discarded backpack and tools in an alley, signaling a missing person in a city where crime is nearly nonexistent.
*   **The Investigation:** A high-ranking officer questions the party but seems to be hiding something. He lies, claiming he will handle it, and urges the party to forget it.
*   **The Mysterious Ally:** The Djinni innkeeper, disguised as a human, gives the party an Amulet of Anti-Detection and later a tracking device, urging them to investigate further.
*   **The Conspiracy:** The party discovers a strange marking on the cloaks of the kidnappers. They learn the kidnappers use teleportation to escape, aided by someone on the inside.
*   **The Trail:** Following the tracker, the party uncovers a trail leading to the swamps far to the west, setting them on the path to a larger conspiracy.

You can use these summaries as standalone campaign outlines or mix and match elements to build your own unique world. For example, the "King's Shadow" plot could be the inciting incident that leads the party to seek answers in the "Celestial Spire," or the urban mystery in "Whispers in the Arcane City" could reveal the first signs of the "Echoes of the Old Gods" conflict. Good luck!

With the first idea, how what could the second arc idea be made to make sure the party stays on the same page with the festival? Make sure you take into account the old man I mentioned, the festival, and the ritual that is planned.

Of course. To ensure the party remains focused on the festival plot in the "King's Shadow" storyline, the second arc can be structured as a two-pronged approach that funnels them toward a single, dramatic conclusion. This design gives players agency while making the festival the undeniable centerpiece of the arc.

Here is a breakdown of the second arc, incorporating the old man, the festival, and the ritual.

### The Second Arc: The Festival of Flesh and Stone

**Goal:** To immerse the party in the vibrant festival, then shatter the illusion with a horrifying ritual, forcing them to become the sole opposition.

---

#### Part 1: Arrival and the Fork in the Road

The party arrives in the capital city by boat and is greeted by the bustling docks and fish market. They hear about the grand festival happening the next day, featuring games, food, and a fighting contest with a prize of a mysterious ring from an old cave system.

At this point, the party has a choice, presenting two distinct paths that both lead to the same destination.

*   **Path A: The Festive Invitation**
    The party decides to attend the festival. They might choose to participate in the fighting contest, enjoy the festivities, and mingle with the crowds. This path allows them to experience the city's culture and build a rapport with its people before the tragedy strikes. They are present at the festival out of curiosity and a desire for reward.

*   **Path B: The Old Man's Warning (The Side Story)**
    Near the docks or marketplace, the party encounters the **suspicious old man**. He is huddled, examining a strange symbol scratched onto a post—one that looks faintly like an eye. He approaches the party (or is approached if they show interest) and shares his theory.
    *   **His Warning:** He tells them he has seen these symbols before and believes something terrible is planned for the festival. He mentions that the city guard is acting strange, with unusual patrol patterns around the festival grounds.
    *   **His Quest:** He gives them a specific task: "The contest's prize is said to be from an old cave system. That cave has been sealed for years. Find it, and you will find the source of this evil." He might give them a crude map or simply point them in the right direction.
    *   **His Motivation:** He can hint that he lost someone in a "tragedy" years ago that bore similar signs, and he cannot bear to watch it happen again.

---

#### Part 2: Convergence on the Festival Grounds

Both paths lead the party to the festival, but with different perspectives.

*   If they took **Path A**, they are already at the festival. They might be preparing for the contest or exploring the stalls.
*   If they took **Path B**, they investigate the cave system. Inside, they find clear evidence of recent ritual activity: ceremonial daggers, chalk drawings of the eye-and-line symbol, and a map of the festival grounds with a large circular zone marked for a "tribute." This discovery confirms the old man's fears and compels them to rush back to the festival to stop whatever is about to happen.

By the evening, regardless of their chosen path, the party is at the festival.

---

#### Part 3: The Climax - The Ritual Begins

As night falls and the festival reaches its peak, the clan you mentioned makes its move. However, it's not just an attack; it's the beginning of the ritual.

1.  **The Distraction:** The clan launches a coordinated assault, targeting the festival's central stage or the contest arena. This serves as a distraction for the guards and the party.
2.  **The Trap is Sprung:** As people flee the initial clash, a section of the festival grounds—likely the one marked on the map in the cave—begins to churn. It turns into the **black quicksand** you described, pulling screaming civilians under. There is no escape except by cutting off the affected area or using powerful magic.
3.  **The Markings Revealed:** The clan members are not just raiders; they are cultists. Their armor and bodies are adorned with the **ovular eye symbol with lines, triangles, and X's**. Party members who fought them earlier might recognize the markings. These markings indicate the number of sacrifices they have performed (| = 10, △ = 100, X = 1000).
4.  **The Objective:** The cultists, led by a charismatic leader, are attempting to expand the ritual zone. They are pushing people toward the black quicksand, trying to complete a massive tribute to their god. The **mysterious ring** from the contest is revealed to be a focus for the ritual, capable of amplifying its power.
5.  **The King's Shadow:** From a high vantage point (perhaps a clock tower or a noble's balcony), the party might spot a figure observing the chaos. Through a spyglass or a successful insight check, they could recognize him as a high-ranking advisor or even **Blank**, the king's friend. His presence implicates him in the plot and sets up the larger conspiracy.

---

#### Why This Keeps the Party on the Same Page

*   **Clear Urgency:** The festival is no longer just a backdrop; it's a ticking time bomb. The black quicksand creates immediate, life-or-death stakes for the NPCs and the party.
*   **Meaningful Choices:** The two paths (attend vs. investigate) cater to different playstyles. The investigation path makes the party feel proactive and clever, while the attendance path lets them experience the world normally before disaster strikes. Both validate their agency.
*   **Convergence:** By having both paths lead to the same climactic scene, you ensure the entire party is united in purpose for the finale, regardless of their initial choices.
*   **Reinforces the Main Plot:** The climax directly showcases the dark ritual, the markings, and introduces the cult's connection to Blank, driving home the central conflict of "The King's Shadow."

This structure uses the festival as a vibrant stage for a horror story, ensuring the players are invested in the event because they are living it, and the old man's side quest provides a compelling alternative route to the same terrifying revelation.

### Review of Blank's Characterization and Inconsistencies

**Blank's Intellectual Profile:**
Based on your notes, Blank is not merely a political schemer; he is a highly intelligent and multifaceted antagonist. His intellectual skills would include:
*   **Grand Strategy:** Successfully maneuvering himself into a position of absolute trust as the king's friend and head of the scouting team implies mastery of court politics, long-term planning, and social manipulation.
*   **Occult Knowledge:** He is the architect of a complex ritual inspired by *Fullmetal Alchemist*, drawing power from sacrifices to emulate the Seven Sins. This requires deep, esoteric knowledge.
*   **Logistical Genius:** Orchestrating a large-scale ritual during a crowded festival, coordinating with a clan, and framing the party suggests exceptional organizational and covert operational skills.
*   **Deceptive Mastery:** He has maintained a facade of loyalty for an extended period, hiding his allegiance to the Dormant Gods from everyone, including a board of directors.

**Logical Inconsistencies in Secrecy:**
While compelling, the current setup has some logical gaps that can be addressed:
1.  **The Scale of the Conspiracy:** A conspiracy involving an entire clan is difficult to keep secret. The risk of a member leaking information is extremely high.
2.  **The High-Risk Venue:** Using a major public festival as the site for a conspicuous ritual (black quicksand, mass sacrifices) is a gamble that seems out of character for a meticulous planner. It's more likely he would choose a more secluded location.
3.  **The Premature Attack:** The party is framed for fighting the clan *at* the festival. If Blank is in control, why would he allow his primary agents to be discovered and engaged in combat before the main ritual? It draws unwanted attention.
4.  **The Nature of the Magic:** The "black quicksand" and large-scale ritual markings are visually spectacular and difficult to conceal or explain away, making a clean getaway or secret operation problematic.

---

### Rewritten Second Arc: The Guardian's Warning

This rewrite re-frames the old man as a key ally, clarifies Blank's plan, and integrates the Dormant Gods and Guardians concepts. It addresses the inconsistencies by making the festival a calculated part of the ritual, not just a lucky opportunity.

**The Setup:**
The party arrives in the capital city. You introduce the "suspicious old man" not as a random citizen, but as **Elian the Scholar**, a renowned historian. He is seen poring over ancient maps and texts in a quiet corner of the marketplace, muttering about constellations and forgotten pantheons.

**Part 1: The Meeting and the Mythos**

*   The party can approach Elian. He is initially wary but becomes animated when they mention the upcoming festival.
*   He reveals he is studying the "Echoes of the Old Gods" (your Dormant Gods concept). He shows them a fragmented stone tablet depicting the **ovular eye symbol with lines and triangles**. He explains that this is the sigil of a forbidden cult that worships the Dormant Gods, beings of primordial chaos who draw power from suffering.
*   He identifies the festival's location as an ancient convergence point for ley lines, a place of immense natural power. He theorizes that the cult plans to use the festival as a massive sacrifice to tear open a rift to the Outer Planes and awaken one of the Dormant Gods.
*   **Elian's True Identity:** He reveals he is one of the **Seven Planewalkers** (your Guardians concept), an ancient guardian sworn to protect the Material Plane from such incursions. He has returned to this city because his divinations showed a critical threat rising. He cannot act directly, as his presence would alert the gods, but he can guide others.
*   He gives the party an **Amulet of Planar Awareness**. When near a follower of the Dormant Gods, it will grow cold and tingle. He also gives them a crude map of the festival grounds, highlighting a section he suspects will be the ritual's focal point.

**Part 2: The Festival's Secret Purpose**

The party learns about the festival and the fighting contest. Elian's research provides a new layer to the contest's prize, the "mysterious ring."
*   The ring is not just from a cave; it's an artifact of the **New Gods** (your orderly deities), a ward against planar chaos. The cult intends to claim it and corrupt it, turning a tool of order into a beacon for their dark god.

**Part 3: The Calculated Provocation**

The party's initial "fight with a clan" is now revealed to be a deliberate act by Blank.
*   Blank allowed the clan to be intercepted. He wanted to gauge the party's strength and see if they could be a potential threat or asset. He may have even orchestrated the encounter to frame them, testing the city's loyalty to the new king.
*   During the festival, the party might spot clan members again. Thanks to Elian's amulet, they can identify them by the faint tingling sensation. Observing these members reveals they are not just thugs; they are fanatics performing small, preparatory rituals.

**Part 4: The Climax - Ritual of the Fallen Star**

As night falls, the main event begins. It is not a chaotic attack, but a chillingly precise ritual.
1.  **The Conduit:** The clan members, led by a powerful priest, move to the section of the festival Elian marked. They are not attacking randomly; they are creating a perimeter.
2.  **The Sacrifice:** They begin herding people toward the center. The black quicksand you described manifests, pulling the victims into a vortex. This is the physical manifestation of the Dormant God's power, fueled by the sacrifices.
3.  **The Focus:** The cultists attempt to seize the ring from the contest's winner, intending to use it to amplify the ritual.
4.  **The Guardian's Intervention:** From the shadows, Elian (the Planewalker) observes. He cannot fight openly, but he can act. He might use his magic to subtly hinder the cultists, create an escape route for NPCs, or send a telepathic warning to the party.
5.  **The Revelation:** As the party fights their way to the center, they might see a figure watching from a high balcony—**Blank**. Through a successful Insight check, they can see his eyes glow with a malevolent, chaotic energy. He is not just influencing the king; he is a vessel for the Dormant God of Sin (e.g., Pride or Wrath), and the ritual is granting him immense power.

**Why This Rewrite Works:**
*   **Integrates All Concepts:** It seamlessly blends the King's Shadow plot with the Dormant Gods, New Gods, and the Planewalker Guardians.
*   **Fixes Inconsistencies:** The festival is not a lucky target but a strategically chosen location. The early fight is a deliberate test. The secrecy is maintained through a mix of political power, cult fanaticism, and the inherent chaos of the Dormant Gods' magic, which is hard to pin down.
*   **Empowers the Old Man:** Elian is no longer a simple quest-giver. He is a powerful, knowledgeable ally whose guidance is crucial. His identity as a Planewalker adds weight and mystery to the conflict.
*   **Raises the Stakes:** The conflict is no longer just about a murder; it's a battle for the very fabric of reality, with the Dormant Gods seeking to reclaim the world.

Here is a complete plan of Blank's actions and the old man's deduction, using only the details from your notes.

### Blank's Grand Plan (Based on Your Notes)

**Phase 1: Consolidation of Power**
*   After the king's murder, Blank, as the late king's good friend and head of the scouting team, positions himself as the protector of the new, naive child king.
*   He joins the board of directors, becoming the king's most influential advisor. His goal is to manipulate the young ruler and use the kingdom's resources for his own ends.

**Phase 2: Co-opting the Clan**
*   Blank is the enemy of the story, and his methods involve emulating the Seven Sins. Your notes state, "The clan and blank do similar stuff... to create markings on ones self."
*   This implies the clan is an independent group already practicing this form of ritualistic tribute. Blank, being highly intelligent, finds them and convinces them to collaborate. He offers them a grand purpose: a massive ritual at the upcoming festival to honor their god and gain immense power.
*   He directs them to perform a preliminary attack at the festival to test security and gauge potential threats (like the party).

**Phase 3: Preparing the Stage**
*   The party arrives in the city and hears about the festival. Blank's plan is already in motion.
*   The clan, under Blank's direction, prepares for the main event. They are not trying to be subtle; they are advertising their presence through attacks and markings.
*   The festival is chosen deliberately. Your notes say the ritual's power "could slightly depend on the party during the festival, as he [Blank] could gain much of his power from sacrifices there." A crowded festival provides the maximum number of potential sacrifices.

**Phase 4: The Festival Ritual**
*   As the festival begins, the clan initiates the ritual. It is not a surprise attack but a calculated move.
*   The ritual works slowly, creating a zone of "black quicksand" that pulls people in. The markings on the clan members (ov-eye with |, △, X) indicate the number of sacrifices they have already performed.
*   The goal is to sacrifice as many people as possible to empower Blank, who is channeling the power of one of the Seven Sins (and possibly a Dormant God). The mysterious ring from the contest is likely intended to be a focus or amplifier for this power.

### The Old Man's Deduction (Based on Your Notes)

The "old man" is not a Planewalker or a secret guardian in your original notes. He is a "suspicious" individual who forms a "hypothesis." His deduction is based on direct observation of the clues Blank's plan inadvertently leaves behind.

1.  **Observation of the Clan:** The old man has likely seen the clan members in the city. He may have witnessed their attack on the party, noticed their distinctive masks and clothes, and perhaps even seen the strange markings (the eye symbol with lines) on their bodies or equipment.
2.  **Knowledge of the Ritual:** Your notes describe the ritual as a "tribute to some god" involving markings. The old man, perhaps being a student of local history or a paranoid observer, recognizes the symbol and understands its significance as a marker of sacrifice.
3.  **Connecting to the Festival:** He hears about the upcoming festival, a large gathering of people. He combines this with his observations: a violent clan known for a sacrificial ritual is in town, and a massive crowd is assembling.
4.  **Forming the Hypothesis:** He logically concludes that the clan intends to use the festival as cover for a large-scale sacrificial ritual. The festival is the perfect venue to maximize the number of sacrifices, which, according to your notes, directly correlates to the power gained by Blank.

His "suspicion" is not a guess; it is a reasoned conclusion based on the evidence. He has seen the actors (the clan), recognized their modus operandi (the markings and ritual), and identified the ideal location (the festival). He then acts on this hypothesis by trying to warn others, leading to the side story that converges with the main plot.

In summary, the plan is not inconsistent. Blank's intelligence lies in his political maneuvering and manipulation of the clan, not in achieving total secrecy. The old man's role is to serve as the audience's exposition, demonstrating how the pieces of the puzzle are visible to those who know what to look for.
